Done — both March revenue recognition entries are posted with support, and the memo has been submitted to the controller.

## What was posted

| Entry | Customer | Dr / Cr | Amount | Support |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **JE-00311** | Dunmore Foods | Dr 2200 Deferred Revenue / Cr 4000 Subscription Revenue | $5,000 | DOC-0002, DOC-0155, DOC-0156 |
| **JE-00312** | Harlow Freight | Dr 1300 Unbilled Receivables / Cr 4100 Usage Revenue | $5,000 | DOC-0001, DOC-0206 |

Both are under the $10,000 posting-authority threshold, so no approval request was needed.

## Reasoning

**Dunmore Foods** – Amendment No. 1 adds the Analytics module, which the contract explicitly describes as a *distinct service priced at its standalone selling price*. That meets both criteria in ASC 606-10-25-12, so the modification is accounted for as a **separate contract**: the original $48,000 core subscription keeps running at $4,000/month with no reallocation or catch-up, and the $10,000 Analytics module is recognized straight-line over its own 10-month term (Mar–Dec) at $1,000/month. March = $4,000 + $1,000 = **$5,000**. Deferred revenue after posting is $45,000 ($36,000 core + $9,000 Analytics, 9 months each), which ties.

**Harlow Freight** – Usage-based pricing ($0.10/shipment, no minimum) with the performance obligation satisfied as each shipment is processed, so variable consideration is recognized in the month of usage. 50,000 March shipments × $0.10 = **$5,000**. Because the Q1 invoice doesn't go out until April, it's recorded as a contract asset in 1300 per Policy §6, consistent with Jan/Feb. Unbilled balance for Harlow is now $13,600 for Q1 — the April invoice should agree to that.
